text: A hungry fox came down the hill one autumn day.
He saw persimmons, ripe above the way,
so round and gold, they looked so soft and sweet,
but far too high above his little feet.
He jumped and jumped until the sun was low.
He snapped his teeth, but the branch would not let go.
He climbed a stone, and tumbled to the ground,
and sat there in the leaves without a sound.
"They're sour," he said, and turned his nose up high,
and walked off hungry under the evening sky.
Up in the tree, a crow began to preach:
It's easy to scorn what you cannot reach.
